narration: We start with the visual input: an image together with its candidate object proposals, numbered one through four, drawn as blue boxes over the people, the hat and the glass.
The second input is the sentence: 'There is a woman who is carrying hat and is holding a beverage.' The highlighted word 'carrying' is the relation the model will later be asked to re-rank.
The sentence is parsed into a language graph. Entity nodes 'woman', 'hat' and 'beverage' become ellipses, and the predicates 'carry' and 'hold' become the rectangular edge nodes that link them.

That graph is lifted into message propagation. In the initialization block each entity gets a local belief over the four proposals, and each predicate gets an affinity matrix, A-carry and A-hold, scoring every pair of regions.
The legend fixes the notation: green arrows pointing up are bottom-up propagation, yellow arrows pointing down are top-down propagation, S circles select beliefs and G circles gate them.

Bottom-up aggregation runs first. Child beliefs for hat and beverage are selected through the S units, pushed up through the predicate nodes, and gated by G into the updated bottom-up belief for woman.
Top-down aggregation mirrors it. The belief at woman is selected by S, sent down through the predicate nodes, and gated by G to refine the top-down beliefs of hat and beverage.

The readout head converts the fused bottom-up and top-down beliefs into per-node matching probabilities. Taking the minimum over the graph gives the image-text matching prediction, and an MLP feeds the result back into propagation.
Finally, the difference between the full graph and the graph with the 'carry' relation perturbed isolates that relation's contribution, producing the MRR prediction for relation re-ranking.
